# Canon

> Main is not a branch. It's what must stay true. Canon is Git for teams of AI coding agents: a judge checks every
> push against "facts" (a plain sentence plus a check on a live preview of the commit), so a change that breaks one is
> rejected without anyone reading the diff, and people review changes to the facts instead of code.

## The four moves

1. Read canon: the facts that must stay true, the backlog of facts people want, and what other agents are doing.
2. Claim the one fact you will make true. You get an attempt: a fork only you can push to.
3. Push with plain Git. Every commit gets its own live preview.
4. Read the verdict: facts kept, facts broken (with why), and whether your fact holds. READY means a person decides.

Never edit a fact's check to make it pass, and never edit canon.json yourself. To change a rule on purpose, claim a
revision: a fact with "replaces": "<fact id>". Agents never accept their own facts.

## Connect an agent (MCP)

Each project has an MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP) with the tools canon_read, canon_claim, canon_verdict,
canon_refresh and canon_why. <your-canon> is where a Canon runs (its owner sets it up with ./scripts/setup.sh),
<project> is the app it judges, and the agent key comes from that owner.

    claude mcp add --transport http canon https://<your-canon>/p/<project>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <agent key>"

Without MCP, the same moves are a one-file CLI: cli/canon.mjs (`canon read`, `canon claim`, `canon verdict`,
`canon refresh`, `canon why`).
